feed.title: Awesome Security & AI Research: a weekly vetted briefing
feed.subtitle: A weekly, source-cited briefing on AI security, product security, and applied AI research. Every finding is vetted, distilled to one lesson and one action, and filed by field. A standing-claims ledger tracks what the field currently believes and what it stopped believing, with the date and reason each answer fell.

entry.title: GPUStack treated spoofable loopback requests as admin, and attackers exploited it
entry.summary: Upgrade GPUStack to 2.2.0 now and treat any AI serving control plane that trusts loopback or a client IP header as unauthenticated.

entry.title: IBM Aspera Faspex authorization bypass gives full admin, exploited in the wild
entry.summary: Patch internet-facing Aspera Faspex 5.0.0 through 5.0.19 per IBM's advisory now and review admin accounts for unexpected changes.

entry.title: Trojanized Claude Code extension on Cursor Marketplace plants persistent SSH backdoor
entry.summary: An AI coding-assistant extension from the official vendor, served by an editor marketplace, ran with full user rights when loaded, so hunt for integrated development environment (IDE) extension hosts writing to ~/.ssh and LaunchAgents and do not treat uninstalling as remediation.

entry.title: Wired says low-skill attackers use AI tools to run ransomware
entry.summary: This headline-level signal matches existing entries on AI-assisted ransomware affiliates and adds no checkable detail.

entry.title: N-able investigates new N-central exploits that work against hotfixed on-premise servers
entry.summary: MSP (managed service provider) teams running on-premise N-central should turn off the Legacy API now, as probing for the new root remote code execution exploit has already been observed.

entry.title: Check Point ships hotfixes for a zero-day exploited for root access
entry.summary: Gateway owners should patch now and hunt for compromise, because attackers chained this flaw with another to reach root and then wipe a VMware ESXi host.

entry.title: Google Project Zero shortens its disclosure deadline to 30 days by 2028
entry.summary: A major research team now treats AI-accelerated exploitation as the default, so vendors need to fix every reported bug within 30 to 60 days and close the patch gap, whatever the bug's severity.

entry.title: PostgreSQL fixes a 22-year-old type confusion bug that enables code execution
entry.summary: Any role that can create objects should be treated as a possible route to code on the database host until the server and its extensions are both upgraded.

entry.title: Attackers chain PHP2Shell and a Gaia root bug to plant TSGA backdoor
entry.summary: If a gateway was exposed, assume the implant survives snapshots and hides in logs, and check it and any ESXi hosts it can reach from outside the appliance.

entry.title: StepSecurity finds fake-interview npm look-alikes stayed on npm for seven months
entry.summary: Interview assignments run on work laptops are an employer supply-chain risk, and the malware hides in build-time code and blockchain-resolved servers that install-script controls and static blocklists both miss.

entry.title: XBOW and Onapsis help uncover 14 SAP NetWeaver vulnerabilities patched in November
entry.summary: Old, rarely reviewed enterprise components often expose functionality without authentication or authorization checks, so SAP NetWeaver owners should patch the critical and missing-authentication notes first.

entry.title: Output-only watermark audits can be evaded by the audited provider
entry.summary: Data-use audits that detect training-data watermarks only through a model's outputs can be defeated by a non-compliant provider that reshapes logits at inference time, leaving weights unchanged and downstream utility largely intact.

entry.title: Poisoned optimizer feedback can plant trigger rules in agent Skills
entry.summary: When agent Skills are rewritten by a text-space optimizer from reference answers, an attacker who poisons only those reference answers can induce a persistent trigger-to-payload rule in the final Skill without access to the model, optimizer or Skill file, while clean accuracy stays close to a benign run.

entry.title: Coding-agent permission files leak secrets into public repositories
entry.summary: Coding agents that persist approved shell commands verbatim (such as Claude Code's .claude/settings.local.json) store any password or token typed in those commands in plaintext project files, and those files are committed to public repositories at measurable rates; format-based secret scanners miss many of these in-command passwords.

entry.title: Constrained decoding wins for structured output, not TOON
entry.summary: For structured model OUTPUT, constrained decoding gives the lowest token usage and plain JSON generation the best accuracy - token-optimized notations do not win here.
